title: How to Nail Intermittent Fasting Macros Without Losing Muscle
description: How to hit protein in a short eating window without losing muscle: evidence-based protein targets, meal structure, carbs around training, common IF mistakes, and accurate logging on compressed days.

body: Intermittent fasting does not cancel protein requirements. If you train and under-eat protein in two meals, you will feel flat and recover worse, even if the scale drops from water and glycogen.
IF can help adherence by shrinking decision windows. It can also hide under-eating protein and total calories if you are not logging the feeding window carefully.

sections.heading: Protein still follows the same ranges
body: Aim for roughly 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg across the day if you lift in a deficit or want to retain muscle. That often means 40 to 60+ g protein per meal when you only eat twice.
A shake is a legitimate tool when chewing volume is the bottleneck. Place protein early in the window so dinner is not an impossible mountain.

sections.heading: Carbs around training
body: If you train inside or near the window, put more carbs around that session for glycogen and performance. Fasted hard training works for some and wrecks others. Use performance as the referee.

sections.heading: Common IF macro mistakes
body: Undershooting protein. Drinking calories in the window without logging. Weekend window drift. Using IF as permission to ignore total energy intake.

sections.heading: Logging compressed days
body: Big meals are exactly when people refuse to open a database. Photo logging helps. Save repeat IF meals to Saved.
IF plus IGNITE AI is a strong combo because those two large meals still get captured when patience is gone.

sections.heading: Bottom line
body: IF is a schedule. Macros are still the content. Hit protein, fuel training, log the window honestly.
